prose.summary: The product meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, which covers doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India‑UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin is CTSH plus VA 45%. CTSH (change in tariff subheading) requires each non‑originating input to be classified in a different six‑digit subheading than the product, while VA (value addition) requires that at least 45% of the product's price, calculated on an FOB basis, does not come from non‑originating materials. The product meets this rule because the final manufacture took place in the UAE, the operations performed go beyond minimal activities, all three non‑originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010, and the build‑down value addition is 49.0%, which exceeds the 45% threshold.

notes.text: The agreement does not clarify whether the build‑down and build‑up methods use the same value‑addition threshold, apart from a 5‑point Ex‑Works adjustment.
For a retrospective certificate, the agreement specifies box 8 for the retrospective mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form require box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

Only for a certificate issued retrospectively: the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
